attempted_axis: Apply the integrator's directional prototype-split advisory to gauntworld.c's atan2 declaration: gauntworld is the LONE f64 dissenter image-wide, so move the outlier onto the consumer-majority f32 spelling (the direction the advisory reports as byte-identical-or-better every time) and measure the one call site's enclosing function.

attributes.law_screen: The prototype lane's directional law (integrator advisory 2026-09-01, 'float-width-prototype-split-is-often-the-shipped-per-tu-shim', in acceptance to main at the time of this pass and therefore cited by name rather than by fetched id) APPLIED and EXERCISED by measurement, in its FAVOURABLE direction: a LONE OUTLIER moving onto the consumer-majority spelling. The advisory's two guards were both honoured - (i) 'never fix a shim in a function that is already exact': the sole call site's enclosing function fn_80060114 was at fuzzy 96.91 / real 293, far from exact, and no exact function in either TU was touched; (ii) 'treat byte-identical as licence-to-keep, not proof-of-right': this change is NOT byte-identical, it is a measured improvement, and it is retained on the combined semantic + measured case set out in the residual, not on the law alone. claim.law.parameter-save-area-width-sets-the-local-block-floor.20260901.v1 SCREENED as the mechanism by which a float-width error is normally invisible in the instruction stream; here the error was NOT slot-invisible because the f64 declaration also forces the return-value conversion, so the change was arbitrated on fndiff --ops rather than slotdiff. The advisory's BB guard (check no fmuls reads the incoming FPR directly) is a guard on the DEFINITION-side lane and does not bind this consumer-side outlier fix. claim.law.insn-count-parity-outranks-local-opcode-fidelity.20260831.v1 SCREENED and is the reason the metric conflict was adjudicated on the diff rather than on the count (see residual).
attributes.residual:
RETAINED IMPROVEMENT. Evidence for the outlier call, gathered before editing: 18 consumer TUs declare `extern f32 atan2(f32 y, f32 x)` (boss, bosscam x2, critter, enemy, combat, controls, gamemain, player, pmotion, mb_objects, pb_objregs, pb_window, ml_fmath, sfx, auxscreen, camera, items); src/game/world/gauntworld.c line 6288 alone declared `extern f64 atan2(f64 y, f64 x)`; and the ACTUAL definition at src/MSL/atanf.c:191 is `f32 atan2(f32 y, f32 x)`. So the majority spelling is also the true one and the dissenter was a genuine ABI defect, not a deliberate per-TU shim - it passed two f32 values as f64 and read an f64 return from a function returning f32. Exactly one call site exists (line 6692, inside fn_80060114), and both of its arguments are already f32 values.

MEASURED: real 293 -> 292, fuzzy 96.9127 -> 97.1905, opcode multiset 5t -> 4t, insns O375 -> O374 against target 378.

METRIC CONFLICT, STATED AND ADJUDICATED ON THE DIFF as the contract requires: the instruction count moved AWAY from the target (deficit 3 -> 4) while real, fuzzy and the multiset all improved. The diff resolves it decisively in favour of keeping. Before the fix the multiset differed in BOTH directions; after it, `--ops` reports `target-only: +1 addi +1 addis +1 mr +1 stfs / ours-only: (none)`. Our instruction stream now contains NO wrong instructions at all - it is a strict subsequence of the target, missing four. That is a strictly healthier residual for future closure than a shorter-but-contaminated stream, and it is why the count regression is accepted here rather than treated as a disqualifier. The four missing instructions are a separate, still-open structural residual in fn_80060114 and were not worked this pass.
